messages.body_plain:
Hi,
You should be able to use those data. You need to create a datetime columns just like the DateTimeOriginal column created by recordTable.

To do that:
1) create a date column by using paste() on year, month day
2) create time column by using paste() on the hours, minutes, second
3) paste date and time to a new column "DateTimeOriginal".

Then you should be able to run the function filterRecordTable() to create independent events.

Best regards,
Jürgen

Within a large cam trap study I m performing with camtrapR, I want to add some data manually, that I managed to recover from corrupted images.
That is, from the corrupted photos I extracted the station number time, date, sps simply by the info displayed in the image, becauset -as the images are corrupt- I can t extract the metadata using camtrapR. Now I want to add those data to the global analysis, merging them with the valid data. Any idea on how to convert that intoI have in excel to the format required by camtrapR?

In other words: I normally use the .csv produced by “record.table” and “write csv” to then do a “survey report”. Now I have 2 sources of data that I want to use to producea “survey report”: 1) the csv from the good photos+ 2) the data in excel. How do I merge 2 with 1?
Thanks a lot,
best regards

Hi,
there is nothing wrong with the format of the metadata in the image. Checked with digiKam and it shows:
2017:01:01 00:00:00
So the format is correct, but the value is wrong.

Two possible explanations for the mismatch in formats:
1) When running recordTable on a folder with only this one image it returns only a date in DateTimeOriginal. So if all images from a camera trap station are affected you may not see the time information. That's a bug due to a very unusual situation
2) Excel may be the culprit again. It likes to auto-format columns and then removes the "uninformative" time 00:00:00.

Either way, there is no usable date/time information in the images, so it is unlikely you can use these images in a straightforward way for most of the usual analyses (apart from confirming presence of species at that location).

Best,
Jürgen

You can use manually created folders,. no problem.
When providing your own path, don't use the system.file() function. It is only for the example. Just give the path as a character string. Copy paste the path from the file explorer is fine (note that on windows one has to exchange the slashes, but not on Linux & Mac).
Spaces in path names are allowed, but generally better avoided… at least for data analysis purposes.

For the other issues I need to know the exact error messages and the code you used.

Thank you,
Jürgen
